papers.title: From RNA design to delivery: Computational strategies for functional RNA therapeutics.
papers.abstract: RNA therapeutics provide a revolutionary means of treating a variety of diseases by precisely regulating gene expression and protein synthesis, with great medical significance. However, there are three key challenges to its clinical application: the inherent instability of RNA, the need for controlled regulation of RNA function, and the lack of an efficient delivery system. Computational strategies provide complementary tools for analyzing and optimizing RNA sequence, structure, function, and delivery, accelerating the rational design of RNAs and the optimization of delivery systems. This revi
papers.summary: This review surveys computational strategies that support the development of RNA therapeutics, covering the design of RNA sequences and structures, control of RNA function, and optimization of delivery systems. It frames these tools as complementary approaches to overcome the instability, regulation, and delivery challenges that limit clinical translation of RNA drugs.

papers.title: Identification of Gene Signatures and Molecular Mechanisms Underlying the Comorbidity of Alzheimer's Disease and Crohn's Disease Using Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Crohn's disease (CD) both involve inflammation and immune dysregulation, yet the potential molecular mechanisms underlying their comorbidity remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study applies machine learning to transcriptomic data to identify shared gene signatures and molecular mechanisms linking Alzheimer's disease and Crohn's disease, two conditions both characterized by inflammation and immune dysregulation. The authors aim to uncover common pathways that could explain their comorbidity and potentially suggest shared therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I from Salvia miltiorrhiza: integrated in vitro and computational evaluation of their antidiabetic potential.
papers.abstract: Salvia miltiorrhiza Bunge (Lamiaceae) is a traditional medicinal plant rich in bioactive tanshinones with diverse pharmacological properties. However, comparative information regarding experimentally measured activity and computational interaction profiles of individual tanshinones remains limited. This study aimed to compare cryptotanshinone (1) and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I (2), isolated from S. miltiorrhiza, using an integrated in vitro and computational approach. The compounds were obtained through activity-informed phytochemical fractionation and evaluated for inhibition of α-glucosidase
papers.summary: This study isolated two tanshinone compounds from Salvia miltiorrhiza and compared their antidiabetic potential using both laboratory enzyme inhibition assays and computational docking analyses. Both cryptotanshinone and 15,16-dihydrotanshinone I showed inhibitory activity against α-glucosidase, a key diabetes drug target, with computational modeling providing insight into their binding interactions.

papers.title: The pod components of the Shigella T3SS sorting platform accommodate multiple copies of Spa33 (SctQ).
papers.abstract: The bacterial type III secretion system (T3SS) uses a membrane-embedded injectisome assembly to export effector proteins into host cells. While atomic-level structural details have been revealed for much of the T3SS apparatus, the model of the cytoplasmic sorting platform remains largely low-resolution. A central structural element of the sorting platform is the so-called "pod" protein, SctQ, which anchors the sorting platform to the inner membrane via interaction with the adaptor protein SctK, and connects to the central ATPase via the spoke protein SctL. SctQ proteins also interact with alte
papers.summary: This study investigates the structural organization of the Shigella type III secretion system sorting platform, focusing on the pod protein Spa33 (SctQ). The authors find that the pod components can accommodate multiple copies of Spa33, providing new insights into how this cytoplasmic platform is assembled. This helps refine the low-resolution model of the sorting platform, which is critical for effector protein export during infection.

papers.title: FuTCM-PDD: a multi-level information fusion framework integrating KAN modeling and AutoML for phenotype-based drug discovery from Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.abstract: Phenotype-based drug discovery has attracted increasing attention due to its critical role in first-in-class drug development and higher clinical translation rates. Chinese Materia Medica (CMM), with its emphasis on properties and efficacies, provides a unique framework for phenotype-oriented therapeutic discovery. We developed an AI-driven framework, FuTCM-PDD, that integrates CMMs, compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, CMM efficacies, and CMM properties to enable phenotype-based drug discovery. For drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) m
papers.summary: FuTCM-PDD is an AI framework that fuses multi-level information (compounds, targets, pathways, pharmacological effects, and Traditional Chinese Medicine properties/efficacies) to support phenotype-based drug discovery. It uses a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for drug-target interaction prediction combined with AutoML, aiming to bridge TCM knowledge with modern phenotype-driven therapeutic discovery.

papers.title: Odorant receptor structures predict the major female sex pheromone component in a moth.
papers.abstract: Species isolation in insects can be ensured by prezygotic barriers, such as species-specific sex pheromone blends that mediate sexual attraction and mate recognition. Yet, sex pheromone compositions of many species remain poorly characterized outside important agricultural pests, because of the necessity to access live insects for pheromone extraction, the difficulties in identifying the production period, and the precise identification of behaviorally relevant compounds in extracts.
papers.summary: This study uses the structures of odorant receptors to predict the major sex pheromone component produced by female moths. By linking receptor structure to pheromone chemistry, the authors provide a computational approach that could identify pheromones in species where live-insect extraction is impractical. This may help characterize species-specific pheromone blends relevant to mate recognition and reproductive isolation.

papers.title: In vitro, in vivo, and computational evaluation of xanthine oxidase inhibitory and antihyperuricemic activities of Piper betle L. ethyl acetate fraction.
papers.abstract: Gout is a metabolic disorder characterized by hyperuricemia and urate crystal deposition. This study evaluated the xanthine oxidase inhibitory, antihyperuricemic, anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and in silico target-binding properties of an EtOAc fraction of Piper betle L. aerial parts.
papers.summary: This study evaluates an ethyl acetate fraction of Piper betle (betel leaf) for its ability to inhibit xanthine oxidase and lower uric acid levels, using in vitro assays, in vivo animal models, and computational docking. The fraction showed antihyperuricemic, anti-inflammatory, and analgesic activities, with in silico analysis suggesting binding to xanthine oxidase and related targets. The findings support the traditional use of Piper betle as a potential natural remedy for gout.

papers.title: Computational prioritization of megalin-aminoglycoside recognition and gentamicin-associated cellular stress responses.
papers.abstract: Aminoglycosides are effective antibiotics for severe infections, but their clinical use is limited by nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity resulting from drug accumulation in non-infected tissues. Megalin, an endocytic receptor expressed in renal proximal tubules and inner-ear tissues, has been proposed as a mediator of this uptake.
papers.summary: This study uses computational methods to investigate how the endocytic receptor megalin recognizes aminoglycoside antibiotics like gentamicin, which accumulate in kidney and inner-ear tissues and cause toxicity. The authors also model the cellular stress responses triggered by gentamicin exposure, aiming to prioritize key molecular interactions that could be targeted to reduce drug toxicity.

papers.title: ProtThermoRank: Sequence-based multi-class prediction model for protein thermal stability changes and its application to CcsZ.
papers.abstract: Protein thermal stability is a key property of industrial enzymes and biopharmaceutical proteins. The rapid and accurate evaluation of thermal stability across large numbers of variants has become a critical step in protein engineering. However, experimental screening of large mutational landscapes remains time-consuming, labor-intensive, and costly. Here, we present ProtThermoRank, a sequence-based multiclass prediction model for mutation-induced changes in protein thermal stability. Unlike existing approaches that encode reference and mutant sequences independently, ProtThermoRank explicitly
papers.summary: ProtThermoRank is a sequence-based multiclass model that predicts how mutations change protein thermal stability, distinguishing itself from prior methods by explicitly encoding reference and mutant sequences together rather than independently. The authors demonstrate its utility by applying it to CcsZ, showing it can rapidly evaluate large mutational landscapes that would otherwise require costly experimental screening.

papers.title: AASIA: A comprehensive protein structural interactome database for agricultural animals.
papers.abstract: Agricultural animals are essential for global food production and sustainable agriculture. Improving disease resistance and economically important traits is critical for ensuring food security. Proteome-wide protein-protein interactions (PPIs), termed as interactomes, underlie key biological processes in cells, making them critical for deciphering the genome-phenome relationship. However, species-specific PPI resources remain limited for most agricultural animals.
papers.summary: AASIA is a new database that catalogs protein-protein interactions across the proteomes of agricultural animals, addressing the lack of species-specific interactome resources for these organisms. By mapping structural interactomes, it aims to help researchers connect genomic variation to traits like disease resistance and economically important phenotypes in livestock.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, in silico studies, and biological evaluation of tosyl-substituted thiazoles, thiazolidin-4-ones, and chromenes as potential anticancer agents.
papers.abstract: A novel series of thiazole, thiazolidin-4-one, and chromene derivatives incorporating a 4-methylbenzenesulfonate (tosylate) moiety were designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their anticancer potential. All structures were elucidated using IR, 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and MS spectroscopy. Anticancer potential was assessed by MTT assay against HepG-2 (hepatocellular carcinoma) and MCF-7 (breast cancer) cell lines, with doxorubicin as a reference. Against MCF-7, compounds 3d (IC50 = 28.2 ± 2.08 µM), 6a (30.0 ± 0.82 µM), and 8a (25.9 ± 1.35 µM) exhibited relatively enhanced cytotoxicity. For HepG-2, de
papers.summary: This paper reports the design, synthesis, and anticancer evaluation of new tosyl-substituted thiazole, thiazolidin-4-one, and chromene compounds. Several derivatives showed moderate cytotoxicity against liver (HepG-2) and breast (MCF-7) cancer cell lines in MTT assays, with the best compounds having IC50 values around 26-30 µM. The work is primarily a medicinal chemistry synthesis and screening study with in silico docking support.

papers.title: Exploring the potential mechanism of Xiaoqinglong Decoction in the treatment of acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease based on network pharmacology and in silico study.
papers.abstract: Xiaoqinglong Decoction (XQLD) is a traditional Chinese herbal formula widely used in clinical practice to treat acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with notable efficacy. Studies indicate that XQLD can effectively modulate the inflammatory response during the acute infectious phase of AECOPD; however, its underlying mechanism of action remains unclear. This study employed network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the potential target genes of XQLD and its possible mechanisms of action in treating AECOPD. Active
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict the targets and mechanisms by which Xiaoqinglong Decoction, a traditional Chinese herbal formula, may treat acute exacerbations of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The authors identify candidate target genes and propose that the formula modulates inflammatory pathways, though findings are computational and lack experimental validation.

papers.title: Spermidine attenuates monocrotaline-induced pulmonary arterial hypertension with HADHA-associated improvements in fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial redox homeostasis.
papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming, impaired mitochondrial quality control, and mitochondrial redox imbalance are increasingly recognized as central drivers of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Spermidine (SPD) has been reported to exert cardiovascular protective effects; however, its effects on endothelial metabolism and redox homeostasis in PAH remain incompletely characterized. HADHA, the α-subunit of mitochondrial trifunctional protein, participates in long-chain fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) and provides a potential link between fatty acid utilization, mitochondrial respiration, mitophagy-relate
papers.summary: This study shows that spermidine supplementation reduces pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) severity in a monocrotaline rat model. The protective effect is linked to HADHA, a mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation enzyme, with improvements in fatty acid oxidation and mitochondrial redox balance. The findings suggest spermidine may help correct metabolic and redox dysfunction in PAH.

papers.title: Cell type-selective targeting by heterobifunctional protein binders via in-cell enrichment.
papers.abstract: Non-catalytic heterobifunctional protein binders promise to expand the range of therapeutic options by establishing complexes between key target proteins and accessory presenter proteins equipped with additional properties. Here, we systematically investigate the rational design of such molecules, explore the biochemical basis of complex formation and determine how they achieve cellular efficacy using the endogenously expressed immunophilin FKBP12 as presenter protein and the transcriptional regulator BRD4 as target protein. We present classes of bifunctional molecules that enable selective, F
papers.summary: This study systematically designs heterobifunctional protein binders that link the endogenous immunophilin FKBP12 to the transcriptional regulator BRD4, forming ternary complexes inside cells. The authors dissect the biochemical rules governing complex formation and show that these molecules can achieve cell type-selective targeting and cellular efficacy. The work provides a rational framework for engineering non-catalytic bifunctional therapeutics.

papers.title: Structure-informed theoretical modeling defines principles governing avidity in bivalent protein interactions.
papers.abstract: In signaling cascades, signaling proteins often encode multiple domains or motifs, which presents the possibility for avidity -- where multivalent binding drastically increases interaction strength and duration. However, predicting and validating multivalent interactions that interact with avidity is a challenge. Here, we integrate mechanistic modeling, structure-based analysis, and experimental approaches as a framework for defining the conditions under which avidity plays a role. We explore the tandem SH2 domain family of interactions with bisphosphorylated partners as a multivalent archetyp
papers.summary: This paper develops a framework combining mechanistic modeling, structure-based analysis, and experiments to predict when avidity—enhanced binding from multivalent interactions—governs bivalent protein interactions. Using tandem SH2 domains binding bisphosphorylated partners as a model system, the authors define the structural and kinetic conditions under which avidity significantly strengthens interaction affinity and duration.

papers.title: TRPM8 virtual screening: the essential role of target-specific, inactive-enriched machine-learning scoring functions.
papers.abstract: The Transient Receptor Potential Melastatin 8 (TRPM8) ion channel is an emerging therapeutic target implicated in pain, inflammation and other disorders. While structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used in drug discovery, the effectiveness of generic and target-specific machine-learning (ML) scoring functions (SFs) for ion channels such as TRPM8 remains to be investigated. We established the first comprehensive structure-based VS benchmark for TRPM8. This evaluates classical docking SFs, generic ML SFs and target-specific ML models retrospectively across multiple TRPM8 protein confo
papers.summary: This study establishes the first comprehensive structure-based virtual screening benchmark for the TRPM8 ion channel, a therapeutic target for pain and inflammation. It compares classical docking scoring functions, generic machine-learning scoring functions, and target-specific ML models, finding that target-specific, inactive-enriched ML scoring functions are essential for effective screening. The work highlights the importance of tailoring ML scoring functions to the specific target rather than relying on generic approaches.

papers.title: Probe-Atom Distributions Obtained from Mixed-Solvent Molecular Dynamics Improve the Scoring of Docking Calculations.
papers.abstract: Structure-based virtual screening (VS) is widely used for the computational selection of drug candidates from compound libraries. Protein-ligand docking calculations are often performed as key steps in the early stages of this process. However, current docking calculations have limited accuracy. Thus, improvements are needed to more efficiently identify promising drug candidates. In this study, we performed mixed-solvent molecular dynamics (MSMD) simulations using four types of probe molecules to improve the accuracy of large-scale VS. We proposed a method for the modification of the docking s
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors use mixed-solvent molecular dynamics simulations with four types of probe molecules to map where small chemical fragments preferentially bind on a protein surface, then incorporate these probe-atom distributions into docking scoring functions. This modification improves the accuracy of large-scale structure-based virtual screening compared to standard docking approaches.

papers.title: PockLigGPT: Pocket-Sequence-Conditioned Molecular Generation with GPTs and RL.
papers.abstract: De novo drug design aims to generate molecules targeting specific protein pockets while retaining chemical plausibility and drug-like properties. Recent 3D structure-based generative methods explicitly model pocket-ligand geometry, but this does not always translate into chemically realistic or practically usable candidate molecules. Molecular language models provide a complementary sequence-based alternative. However, it remains unclear whether sequence-based pocket information can effectively guide ligand generation, whether multistage training improves pocket-specific generation, and whethe
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: PockLigGPT introduces a GPT-based molecular generation model conditioned on protein pocket sequences, combined with reinforcement learning to improve pocket-specific ligand design. The work investigates whether sequence-based pocket information (rather than 3D geometry) can effectively guide generation of chemically plausible, drug-like molecules, and whether multistage training improves results. It offers a complementary approach to 3D structure-based generative methods for de novo drug design.

papers.title: Defect-Engineered Tetragonal ZrO2 Nanoparticles for Biomaterial Interfaces: Green Synthesis, Biointerfacial Interactions, and SERS Biosensing.
papers.abstract: Zirconia (ZrO2) is a widely used biomaterial in dental and orthopedic applications due to its excellent biocompatibility, chemical stability, and mechanical properties. However, the role of defect structure and phase composition in governing biomolecule-surface interactions at the biointerface remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we demonstrate a synthesis-driven strategy for engineering defect-rich tetragonal ZrO2 nanoparticles via conventional wet-chemical and plant-extract-mediated green routes using Laurus nobilis, Salvia rosmarinus, and Ficus benghalensis. Plant-mediated synth
papers.summary: This paper reports a green synthesis route for defect-rich tetragonal ZrO2 nanoparticles using plant extracts (Laurus nobilis, Salvia rosmarinus, Ficus benghalensis), comparing them to conventionally synthesized particles. The study examines how defect structure and phase composition influence biomolecule-surface interactions at the biointerface and explores their use in SERS-based biosensing. The work aims to link synthesis-driven defect engineering to improved biomaterial interface performance.

papers.title: Structural Overview of GLP-1 Analogs.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) analogs exert potent metabolic effects through structural features that govern receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. Key structural determinants include N-terminal modifications that confer resistance to dipeptidyl peptidase-4 degradation, as well as C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize peptide helicity and enhance GLP-1 receptor affinity. Lipidation and albumin-binding strategies prolong systemic exposure by increasing circulating half-life, forming the basis of long-acting agents such as liraglutide and semaglutide. Structural variat
papers.summary: This review examines how the structural features of GLP-1 analogs—such as N-terminal modifications that resist DPP-4 degradation, C-terminal and backbone elements that stabilize helicity, and lipidation strategies that extend half-life—determine their receptor engagement, signaling, and pharmacokinetics. These structural insights explain the design basis of long-acting agents like liraglutide and semaglutide.

papers.title: Covalent Stabilizers of the Interaction Between 14-3-3σ and Estrogen Receptor‑α.
papers.abstract: Selective stabilization of complexes formed by the hub protein 14-3-3 represents an emerging mechanism for the modulation of therapeutically relevant targets. In this letter, we describe a hit-finding campaign designed to identify small molecule stabilizers of the interaction between 14-3-3σ and the estrogen receptor alpha (ERα). Four structurally distinct hits were identified and validated using a combination of biochemical assays and biophysical techniques. Ternary complex crystal structures revealed that all four hit compounds form a covalent bond with Cys38 of 14-3-3σ via four different el
papers.summary: This paper reports the discovery of four structurally distinct small molecules that stabilize the interaction between the hub protein 14-3-3σ and estrogen receptor alpha (ERα). Crystal structures of the ternary complexes show that all four compounds covalently bind to Cys38 of 14-3-3σ, revealing a new mechanism for modulating ERα activity. This represents an early-stage hit-finding effort toward covalent stabilizers of protein-protein interactions.

papers.title: Decoding co-encapsulation of β-carotene and tocopherol in zein nanoparticles through orthogonal spectroscopy and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Protein-based nanoparticles (NPs), particularly zein NPs, are increasingly explored as oral carriers for nutrients and nutraceuticals due to their affordability, functionality, biodegradability, and biocompatibility. Co-encapsulation strategies can improve encapsulation efficiency and enhance the chemical stability of labile bioactive compounds; however, understanding the intermolecular interactions governing these systems remains challenging. In this study, zein NPs co-loaded with tocopherol (TC) and β-carotene (βC) at different ratios were investigated using Fourier Transform Infrared, fluor
papers.summary: This study investigates how zein nanoparticles co-encapsulate two bioactive compounds, β-carotene and tocopherol, at varying ratios. Using FTIR, fluorescence spectroscopy, and machine learning, the authors decode the intermolecular interactions that govern encapsulation efficiency and stability. The work provides a framework for designing better nutrient delivery systems.

papers.title: Enhancing biocatalytic retrosynthesis with a graph-to-graph model.
papers.abstract: Biocatalytic synthesis offers a green and sustainable route for chemical production, yet the rational design of biocatalytic routes remains challenging due to the need to jointly consider reaction feasibility and enzymatic compatibility. Here, we present BioG2G_ESR, a unified framework centered on graph-to-graph modeling for single-step biocatalytic retrosynthesis, with enzyme sequence recommendation as a downstream extension. BioG2G formulates retrosynthesis as a graph-to-graph translation task, directly predicting reactant molecular graphs from product structures while preserving molecular t
papers.summary: The authors present BioG2G_ESR, a graph-to-graph deep learning framework that predicts reactant molecular graphs directly from product structures for single-step biocatalytic retrosynthesis, with enzyme sequence recommendation as a downstream task. By jointly modeling reaction feasibility and enzymatic compatibility, the method aims to make rational design of biocatalytic synthesis routes more tractable.

papers.title: Rational Design of Au@co-MOF Synergistic Platform for Ultrasensitive Monitoring of Dopamine in Human Biological Fluids.
papers.abstract: This study presents the rational design and application of engineered metal-organic framework (MOF) hybrids, tailored to exhibit accelerated electron transfer kinetics and enhanced molecular recognition capabilities for the high-sensitivity detection of dopamine (DA). Specifically, an enzyme-free electrochemical sensing platform was constructed using Au@Co-MOF nanocomposites, which were synthesized via a controllable in situ growth approach. Au nanoparticles (AuNPs) were uniformly anchored onto the [Co3(TMA)3(H2O)5]n (where TMA = 1,3,5-trimesic acid) framework containing coordinatively unsatur
papers.summary: This study reports an enzyme-free electrochemical sensor built from gold nanoparticle-decorated cobalt metal-organic framework (Au@Co-MOF) composites for detecting dopamine in human biological fluids. The engineered hybrid shows accelerated electron transfer and improved molecular recognition, enabling ultrasensitive dopamine quantification. The platform is positioned as a practical tool for clinical monitoring of dopamine-related disorders.

papers.title: In Silico Identification of Novel Leads as Potential DPP-IV Inhibitors as Antidiabetic Agents Using Virtual Screening.
papers.abstract: Purpose: Dipeptidyl peptidase-IV (DPP-IV) is a validated therapeutic target for type 2 diabetes mellitus due to its role in incretin hormone degradation. This study aimed to identify novel small-molecule DPP-IV inhibitors from the ECBD database using an integrated virtual screening and molecular dynamics (MD) approach, acknowledging that experimental validation is necessary to confirm biological activity. Methods: Structure-based virtual screening of 5,500 ECBD compounds was performed using molecular docking to identify high-affinity ligands, followed by interaction analysis with key catalytic
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen 5,500 compounds from the ECBD database for potential inhibitors of DPP-IV, a validated target for type 2 diabetes. Several high-affinity lead compounds were identified through interaction analysis with key catalytic residues, though the authors note that experimental validation is required to confirm biological activity.

papers.title: Drug Design Studio (DDS) 2.0: A Unified Platform for Network Pharmacology Integrated with Docking and Virtual Screening Workflow for Covalent/Non-Covalent Binders.
papers.abstract: Network pharmacology has become a central paradigm in modern drug discovery, replacing the reductionist "one drug, one target" view with a systems-level understanding of how compounds engage networks of proteins that are linked to disease. Despite its impact, a typical network-pharmacology study remains fragmented and technically demanding: researchers must query several independent databases, install and reconcile multiple standalone tools for target collection, network construction, hub-gene ranking and pathway enrichment, and then manually bridge the results into structure-based follow-up s
papers.summary: DDS 2.0 is a unified software platform that integrates network pharmacology with molecular docking and virtual screening, allowing researchers to go from compound-target network analysis to structure-based screening of covalent and non-covalent binders in one workflow. It addresses the fragmentation of typical network pharmacology studies, which currently require juggling multiple databases and standalone tools.

papers.title: A resource-efficient structure-based workflow for fragment progression enables parallel hit discovery and validation of functionally diverse modulators of NCS-1 protein-protein interactions.
papers.abstract: Efficient drug discovery workflows ideally generate data that directly address key translational milestones, including confirmation of target engagement and binding pose, structure-activity relationships (SARs), and biological relevance, within rapid and resource-efficient experimental cycles. Here, we describe a data-driven, automation-assisted, customizable framework for fragment-to-hit progression that directly delivers structurally validated hit series primed for rapid SAR exploration by exploiting the high-throughput crystallography available at synchrotrons. This recently evolved direct-
papers.summary: The authors present a resource-efficient, structure-based workflow that uses high-throughput synchrotron crystallography to rapidly progress fragments into validated hit compounds. Applied to the NCS-1 protein, the approach yielded functionally diverse modulators of its protein-protein interactions while confirming target engagement and binding poses. The framework is customizable and designed to accelerate hit discovery with minimal resources.

papers.title: Substrate Recognition Analysis in an Ethyl Carbamate-Hydrolyzing Esterase and Semi-Rational Baijiu Flavor Preservation.
papers.abstract: Ethyl carbamate (EC) is a widely recognized carcinogen present in fermented foods, and enzymatic degradation is a safe and effective strategy for its reduction. An EC-degrading esterase derived from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus (AcECH) was previously identified. However, volatile ester compounds in Chinese Baijiu compete with EC for enzyme binding, thereby affecting degradation efficiency and flavor quality. In this study, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, enzyme kinetics, bio-layer interferometry (BLI), and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) were employ
papers.summary: This study investigates how an ethyl carbamate-degrading esterase (AcECH) from Acinetobacter calcoaceticus interacts with volatile ester compounds found in Chinese Baijiu, which compete with the carcinogen for enzyme binding. Using molecular docking, MD simulations, enzyme kinetics, BLI, and GC-IMS, the authors characterize substrate recognition and propose a semi-rational strategy to preserve Baijiu flavor while reducing ethyl carbamate. The work offers a practical enzymatic approach to improving food safety in fermented beverages without compromising aroma.

papers.title: AlloPool is a deep learning framework that infers protein allostery from molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence have transformed protein structure prediction and design. However, protein function is governed not only by static structures but also by the conformational dynamics that allow proteins to access distinct functional states. Predicting these dynamic transitions, central to many biological processes, remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-resolution experimental data, which limits the training of machine-learning models for dynamic and energetic property prediction. Here, we present AlloPool, a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that in
papers.summary: AlloPool is a graph neural network framework that predicts protein allostery—how binding at one site affects function at a distant site—by learning from molecular dynamics simulations. It addresses the scarcity of experimental data on protein conformational dynamics by leveraging simulated trajectories to train models that infer dynamic and energetic properties. This offers a new computational route to understanding protein function beyond static structures.

papers.title: Phytochemical Profiling and Biological Evaluation of Pistacia lentiscus L. grown in Chlef (Algeria): An Integrated In Vitro, In Vivo, and In Silico Study.
papers.abstract: Pistacia lentiscus L. plays an integral role in Algerian traditional therapy. The aim of this study was to evaluate P. lentiscus methanol extract (PLME) for its potential antihypoxic and antioxidant activity and to characterize its phytochemical profile. Locomotor and exploratory behavior were investigated using the open-field test (OF). Also, biological activity prediction was performed using the PASS online platform, and molecular docking studies were carried out using AutoDock Vina software. Quantitative investigations revealed high levels of total phenolics (713.952 ± 12.58 mg GAE/g extrac
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phytochemical profile of a methanol extract from Pistacia lentiscus grown in Chlef, Algeria, and evaluates its antioxidant and antihypoxic activity using in vitro, in vivo (mouse open-field test), and in silico (PASS prediction and molecular docking) approaches. The extract showed high total phenolic content and promising biological activity, with docking suggesting potential molecular targets.

papers.title: Chemical Characterization and Pharmacological Activity of Byrsonima crassifolia (L.) Kunth (Murici): Antinociceptive Effects, Edema Reduction, and Molecular Docking.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the chemical composition, anti-inflammatory and antinociceptive activities of murici leaf (ELM) and bark (EBM) extracts using adult zebrafish (Danio rerio). HPLC analysis identified rutin, isoquercitrin, and kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside as the major phenolic compounds. Both extracts exhibited low toxicity and no sedative effects at the lowest tested doses. ELM showed abdominal antinociceptive activity mediated by TRPA1 and significantly reduced carrageenan-induced abdominal edema. EBM inhibited both corneal (TRPV1) and abdominal (TRPA1) nociception, producing effects simil
papers.summary: This study characterizes the phenolic composition of murici (Byrsonima crassifolia) leaf and bark extracts, identifying rutin, isoquercitrin, and kaempferol-3-O-rutinoside as major compounds. Using zebrafish models, the extracts showed low toxicity and antinociceptive and anti-edema effects mediated through TRPA1 and TRPV1 pathways, with molecular docking supporting the observed bioactivities. The work provides preclinical evidence for the traditional medicinal use of murici as an anti-inflammatory and analgesic agent.

papers.title: In Vitro Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Sour Cherry (Prunus cerasus L.) Seed Oil and Computational Safety Profiling.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the in vitro anti-inflammatory activity of sour cherry seed oils, including samples obtained by Soxhlet extraction and maceration, as well as ten commercial samples. The results demonstrated that the 15-lipoxygenase inhibitory activity of the oil samples ranged from 6% to 80%. Regarding cyclooxygenase (COX) inhibition, while most samples showed negligible activity, the oil produced by Soxhlet extraction inhibited COX-1 and COX-2 by 38% and 32%, respectively. Similarly, the oil obtained via maceration showed inhibition rates of 25% and 23% for COX-1 and COX-2, respe
papers.summary: This study evaluated the anti-inflammatory properties of sour cherry seed oils from different extraction methods and commercial sources, finding that 15-lipoxygenase inhibition ranged widely from 6% to 80%, while COX-1 and COX-2 inhibition was generally weak except for Soxhlet-extracted oil (38% and 32%, respectively). The authors also performed computational safety profiling of the oils.

papers.title: Computational and Comparative In Vitro Evaluation of GC-MS Profiled Cannabis sativa Inflorescence Extracts' Metabolites on Selected Diabetes Therapeutic Targets.
papers.abstract: Cannabis sativa, a medicinal plant rich in cannabinoids, terpenoids, and flavonoids, has been shown to have various pharmacological activities. This study investigated the antidiabetic potential of C. sativa inflorescence extracts using in vitro and computational models. Dried C. sativa inflorescences were extracted sequentially with hexane, dichloromethane, and methanol, before their metabolites were identified by GC-MS. The extracts were tested for α-amylase and α-glucosidase inhibition, glucose uptake activity, and antioxidant effects using DPPH and nitric oxide (NO) inhibition assays. Thir
papers.summary: This study profiled metabolites from Cannabis sativa inflorescence extracts using GC-MS and tested them for antidiabetic activity through in vitro enzyme inhibition assays (α-amylase, α-glucosidase), glucose uptake, and antioxidant assays, complemented by computational docking against diabetes-related targets. The extracts showed measurable inhibitory and antioxidant activities, with specific cannabinoids, terpenoids, and flavonoids implicated as likely bioactive contributors.

papers.title: Design, Synthesis, Antimycobacterial Evaluation, and In Silico Investigation of Benzisothiazole-Based Hydrazide Derivatives as Potential Anti-Tuberculosis Agents.
papers.abstract: A series of novel benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives was rationally designed, synthesized, and evaluated for their antitubercular activity. Among the synthesized compounds, derivative 8k emerged as the most potent candidate, exhibiting a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 0.25 μg/mL, along with a high selectivity index (SI) of 42 and confirmed bactericidal activity. To gain preliminary insights into its possible mechanism of action, compound 8k was subjected to molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, using enoyl-acyl carrier protein reductase (InhA) as the
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized a series of benzisothiazole-based hydrazide derivatives and tested them against tuberculosis bacteria. The most potent compound, 8k, showed strong activity (MIC 0.25 μg/mL), good selectivity, and bactericidal effects, with docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggesting it may target the InhA enzyme. These findings highlight a promising new scaffold for anti-TB drug development.

papers.title: The impact of TcdB conformational dynamics on vaccination against Clostridioides difficile.
papers.abstract: Clostridioides difficile TcdB is a multidomain ~270 kDa protein that adopts at least two distinct structural conformations influencing receptor binding, sensitivity to bile salts, and antibody reactivity. Data from the current study suggest TcdB may benefit from conformational flexibility by avoiding neutralization by vaccine induced antibodies. Experiments further demonstrate that targeting a single TcdB conformation overcomes the toxin's ability to evade antibody neutralization. In the first series of experiments, mice were administered TcdB engineered with a 19 amino acid deletion and two s
papers.summary: This study shows that the C. difficile toxin TcdB can adopt multiple structural conformations, which helps it evade antibodies generated by vaccination. By targeting a single specific conformation of TcdB, researchers were able to overcome the toxin's immune evasion and achieve effective neutralization in mice. This suggests that conformation-specific vaccine design could improve protection against C. difficile infection.

papers.title: Cannabis as a source of novel therapeutics: A computational study combining LBDD and structure-based docking/dynamics to identify novel drug-like compounds for colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Cannabis represents a valuable source of bioactive compounds with significant therapeutic potential, thanks to its rich phytochemical profile, making it a prime candidate for cancer research. Our study investigates the potential of cannabis-derived compounds to inhibit cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2), a crucial regulator of cell-cycle progression and colorectal cancer cell proliferation. A comprehensive computational workflow integrating 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, drug-likeness assessment, and ADMET prediction was employed to investigate a dataset of
papers.summary: This computational study screened cannabis-derived phytochemicals for their ability to inhibit CDK2, a cell-cycle kinase implicated in colorectal cancer proliferation. Using 3D-QSAR modeling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET/drug-likeness predictions, the authors identified candidate compounds with favorable binding and pharmacokinetic profiles. The work proposes cannabis as a source of novel drug-like CDK2 inhibitors warranting further experimental validation.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven identification of PIM2 kinase inhibitors through QSAR modeling and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The proto-oncogene serine/threonine kinase PIM2 is a critical regulator of cell proliferation, survival, and tumor progression and represents an attractive therapeutic target for several cancers. In this study, an integrated machine learning-guided computational pipeline was developed to identify potential PIM2 inhibitors by combining quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, and pharmacokinetic prediction. Bioactivity data for PIM2 inhibitors were retrieved from the ChEMBL database, yielding 5953 co
papers.summary: This study developed an integrated computational pipeline combining machine learning-based QSAR modeling, virtual screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to identify potential PIM2 kinase inhibitors for cancer therapy. Using 5,953 bioactivity data points from ChEMBL, the authors built predictive models and screened compound libraries to prioritize candidate inhibitors with favorable pharmacokinetic properties.

papers.title: Structure-based identification of small-molecule stabilizers targeting mutant TP53 (Y220C) in breast cancer: a pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking and dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Mutations in TP53, particularly the Y220C variant, destabilize the protein and impair tumor-suppressor function, driving breast cancer progression. Restoring the structural integrity of TP53 Y220C using small-molecule stabilizers represents a potential therapeutic strategy.
papers.summary: This study uses computational approaches—pharmacophore modeling, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations—to identify small molecules that could stabilize the mutant TP53 Y220C protein, a common cancer-driving mutation in breast cancer. The goal is to find compounds that restore the tumor-suppressor function lost when this mutation destabilizes p53's structure.

papers.title: Structure-based virulence factor classification using a dual-driven graph transformer with a pretrained language model.
papers.abstract: Bacterial pathogenicity relies on a multitude of virulence factors (VFs). Identifying these factors is crucial for comprehending the molecular mechanisms driving bacterial pathogenesis and pinpointing potential targets for antivirulence strategies. While the identification of VFs has received extensive attention, there is still a lack of prediction from the perspective of VF classes. Moreover, most computational methods focus solely on sequence information for virulence proteins, neglecting spatial structure information. Here, a novel Structure-based Dual-driven Graph Transformer framework nam
papers.summary: The paper introduces a structure-based dual-driven graph transformer framework that incorporates a pretrained protein language model to classify bacterial virulence factors into specific functional classes. By combining sequence-derived embeddings with spatial structural information, the method aims to improve prediction of virulence factor categories, which could aid in understanding bacterial pathogenesis and identifying antivirulence targets.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "Computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as potential aromatase inhibitors: Molecular docking, ADMET, Network pharmacology, Molecular dynamics simulation, and DFT studies" [Pharmaceutic. Sci. Adv. 4 (2026) 100108].
papers.abstract: [This corrects the article DOI: 10.1016/j.pscia.2026.100108.].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum correcting the original article on computational screening of Sophora flavescens phytochemicals as aromatase inhibitors. It does not present new scientific findings, only corrections to the previously published work.

papers.title: Computational evaluation of EPA-PC binding to GCase in neuronopathic Gaucher disease.
papers.abstract: Gaucher disease (GD) is a lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient acid β-glucosidase (GCase) activity and consequent accumulation of glucosylceramide. Current enzyme replacement and substrate reduction therapies improve several systemic manifestations but have limited impact on neuronopathic disease, motivating evaluation of alternative molecular strategies. This study computationally assessed the interaction of EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, with human GCase (PDB ID: 2NSX). The protein structure was examined by Ramachandran analysis and hydroph
papers.summary: This study uses computational docking and molecular dynamics to evaluate how EPA-phosphatidylcholine (EPA-PC), a marine-derived omega-3 phospholipid, binds to the lysosomal enzyme GCase, which is deficient in Gaucher disease. The work explores whether this interaction could offer an alternative molecular strategy for neuronopathic forms of the disease that respond poorly to current therapies. Findings are preliminary and based entirely on in silico modeling.

papers.title: The substrate envelope strategy: Structural basis for resistance mitigation in antiviral drug design.
papers.abstract: Drug resistance remains a major hurdle in antiviral drug development. This review highlights the "substrate envelope hypothesis", a structure-based drug design (SBDD) paradigm that constrains the spatial boundaries and binding footprint of inhibitors within the conserved active site volume defined by natural viral substrates. By restricting inhibitor interactions to evolutionarily conserved residues, this approach ensures that mutations abrogating drug binding simultaneously impair natural substrate processing. This imposes an insurmountable fitness cost on the virus, thereby mitigating resist
papers.summary: This review describes the substrate envelope hypothesis, a structure-based drug design strategy that confines antiviral inhibitors to the conserved active-site volume occupied by natural viral substrates. By targeting evolutionarily conserved residues, mutations that weaken drug binding also impair substrate processing, imposing a fitness cost that limits resistance. The paper synthesizes structural evidence supporting this paradigm for antiviral development.

papers.title: HDX-MS-Guided computational modeling for rapid and accurate antibody-antigen interface mapping.
papers.abstract: Accurate mapping of paratopes and epitopes at antibody-antigen (Ab-Ag) interfaces is essential for the rational design of therapeutic antibodies in early drug development. Traditional methods for determining high-resolution Ab-Ag complex structures, such as X-ray crystallography and cryo-electron microscopy, are labor-intensive and require substantial time and resources. Although recent computational approaches have increased throughput, prediction accuracy and reliability remain limited, particularly without experimental structural constraints. Here, we present a hydrogen-deuterium exchange m
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational workflow that uses hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) data as experimental constraints to guide antibody-antigen interface modeling. The approach aims to rapidly and accurately map paratopes and epitopes, addressing the cost and time limitations of crystallography and cryo-EM while improving on purely computational predictions.

papers.title: All-atom molecular dynamics simulation of Cyclophilin A in complex with Sanglifehrin A.
papers.abstract: Cyclophilin A (CypA), a key peptidyl-prolyl cis/trans isomerase, plays a pivotal role in various biological processes and is a target for therapeutic intervention, particularly in viral and cancer-related diseases. This study explores the structural and dynamic effects of Sanglifehrin A (SangfA), a potent CypA inhibitor, using molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. All-atom MD simulations (100 ns) of apo CypA and its complex with SangfA were performed using GROMACS v2023. In addition to MD analyses, essential dynamics, clustering, secondary structure, and binding free energy were analyzed. SangfA
papers.summary: This study uses 100 ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to compare apo Cyclophilin A with its complex with the inhibitor Sanglifehrin A. The authors analyze structural dynamics, essential motions, clustering, secondary structure, and binding free energy to characterize how SangfA binding affects CypA. The work provides atomistic insight into the interaction between this peptidyl-prolyl isomerase and a potent inhibitor.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based structural modeling of PSTOL1 receptor kinases in rice and sorghum.
papers.abstract: Originally identified in rice (Oryza sativa OsPSTOL1), PHOSPHORUS-STARVATION TOLERANCE 1 (PSTOL1) proteins are essential determinants of phosphorus efficiency in several plant species, including Sorghum bicolor (SbPSTOL1). In contrast to OsPSTOL1, SbPSTOL1 homologs exhibit a transmembrane receptor-like kinase (RLK) architecture with polymorphic extracellular domains. We employed an AI-driven computational pipeline to investigate the structure and conformational dynamics of SbPSTOL1 proteins. Monomeric predictions using multiple deep-learning platforms yielded structures that were inconsistent
papers.summary: This study applies AI-based protein structure prediction tools to model PSTOL1 receptor kinases from rice and sorghum, which are key determinants of phosphorus-use efficiency in crops. The authors find that monomeric predictions from multiple deep-learning platforms produce inconsistent structures, particularly for the polymorphic extracellular domains of sorghum homologs, highlighting limitations in current modeling approaches for these receptor-like kinases.

papers.title: Design and syntheses of 4-aminoquinoline-thiazolidinone hybrids as anti-protozoal agents.
papers.abstract: Molecular hybridization is an effective approach employed to synthesize molecules that possess the ability to function as dual inhibitors, thereby addressing the issue of growing resistance. Resistance by the malaria parasite is one such example. Therefore, the study aims to develop hybrid compounds consisting of 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone, utilizing molecular docking for sorting, followed by synthesis and evaluation of their anti-malarial potential.
papers.summary: This study designed and synthesized hybrid molecules combining 4-aminoquinoline and 4-thiazolidinone scaffolds, using molecular docking to prioritize candidates before synthesis. The hybrids were then evaluated for anti-malarial activity, aiming to create dual-inhibitor compounds that could overcome parasite resistance.

papers.title: Structural Prerequisites for Pim-1 Kinase Inhibition and the Identification of a Pyrazolyl-Methylene-Indolinone Hit.
papers.abstract: Pim-1 is a serine/threonine kinase of the pan-Pim family (Pim-1, -2, and -3), whose overexpression is associated with various cancers. Its distinctive hinge-region architecture provides opportunities for selective inhibitor development, with several inhibitors reported as clinical candidates. Understanding structure-activity relationships is essential for distinguishing biologically active compounds from high-scoring docking hits, a major challenge in structure-based drug discovery.
papers.summary: This paper analyzes the structural requirements for inhibiting Pim-1 kinase, a cancer-associated serine/threonine kinase, and identifies a new pyrazolyl-methylene-indolinone compound that hits the target. The work highlights how Pim-1's distinctive hinge region can be exploited for selective inhibitor design and emphasizes the need to distinguish true actives from misleading docking scores in structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: Identification of key genes and metabolites in thyroid eye disease through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Thyroid eye disease (TED) markedly compromises ocular function and quality of life, imposing significant healthcare and economic burdens. Present therapeutic strategies, which mainly include glucocorticoids, teprotumumab, immunosuppressive drugs, and surgical treatments, exhibit limited effectiveness and are associated with high rates of relapse. Consequently, unraveling the molecular mechanisms of TED and discovering new diagnostic and therapeutic targets hold immense clinical importance.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic and metabolomic data to identify key genes and metabolites involved in thyroid eye disease (TED), aiming to uncover molecular mechanisms behind the disease. The findings highlight potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets that could improve on current limited and relapse-prone treatments. The work provides a multi-omics framework for understanding TED pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrative computational approach to elucidate the efficacy of cordyceps in managing lupus nephritis: from molecular targets to clinical applications.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in immunosuppressive therapies, lupus nephritis (LN) continues to be a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. The scarcity of reliable biomarkers for predicting renal outcomes further complicates clinical management. While Cordyceps is recognized for its immunomodulatory properties as a medicinal fungus, its therapeutic potential in LN remains underexplored. Moreover, it is unclear whether its molecular targets identified through screening constitute viable therapeutic interventions for this disease.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrative computational approach to investigate whether Cordyceps, a medicinal fungus with immunomodulatory properties, could be effective in treating lupus nephritis. The authors screen for molecular targets of Cordyceps and connect them to clinical applications, aiming to identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic interventions for this kidney complication of lupus.

papers.title: Computational insights into synergistic mechanisms of PD-901 and 5-azacitidine targeting PTPN11 (SHP2) E76K mutation in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia.
papers.abstract: Juvenile Myelomonocytic Leukemia (JMML) is an aggressive pediatric hematological cancer categorized by aberrant activation of the RAS/MAPK pathway. It is commonly caused by gain-of-function mutations, such as E76K in the PTPN11 protein. While 5-azacitidine (5-Aza) and the MEK inhibitor PD0325901 (PD-901) are not known direct inhibitors of SHP2/PTPN11, the reported activity of 5-Aza combined with MEK inhibition in PTPN11-mutated JMML offered a biological rationale for examining their potential structural interactions with SHP2.
papers.summary: This computational study investigates how 5-azacitidine and the MEK inhibitor PD-901 might interact with the SHP2/PTPN11 E76K mutant protein that drives juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia. Using molecular docking and simulation approaches, the authors explore potential binding interactions that could explain the reported clinical activity of this drug combination. The work provides structural hypotheses for why these drugs, though not classical SHP2 inhibitors, may synergize in PTPN11-mutated JMML.

papers.title: Repurposed metformin-apigenin combination therapy for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: from integrative multi-omics discovery to in vivo validation.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) is a chronic liver disease. Although recent drugs have been approved, the complex pathophysiology of MASH limits monotherapy efficacy and generates considerable inter-patient heterogeneity. The purpose of this research was to identify new molecular targets and develop a rational combination therapeutic approach for MASH.
papers.summary: This study used integrative multi-omics analysis to identify molecular targets for MASH and proposed a repurposed combination of metformin and apigenin as a rational therapy. The combination was then validated in vivo, suggesting a promising multi-target strategy for a disease with complex pathophysiology and limited monotherapy efficacy.

papers.title: From drug export to envelope fitness: characterizing the regulatory landscape of selective Escherichia coli ABC efflux pumps.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance remains a top global health threat. While ATP-binding cassette (ABC) efflux pumps contribute to multidrug resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, their transcriptional regulation is far less understood than that of the RND and MFS families.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the transcriptional regulatory landscape of selective ABC efflux pumps in Escherichia coli, a family whose regulation is poorly understood compared to RND and MFS transporters. It links these pumps not only to drug export but also to envelope fitness, expanding their functional roles beyond multidrug resistance.

papers.title: Integrated analysis of isorhamnetin-associated targets in chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer: immune-infiltration associations and antitumor effects in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.abstract: Chronic pancreatitis (CP) creates an inflammatory pancreatic microenvironment and is an established risk factor for pancreatic cancer (PC). However, immune-inflammatory links between CP and PC remain unclear. Isorhamnetin (ISO), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antitumor activities, may influence pancreatic inflammatory signaling. This study investigated ISO-associated molecular networks shared by CP and PC, examined the relationships between prioritized targets and transcriptome-estimated immune-cell infiltration, and evaluated the effects of ISO in pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.summary: This study used integrated bioinformatics to identify molecular targets shared between chronic pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer that are associated with the flavonoid isorhamnetin, and linked these targets to immune cell infiltration patterns. Experimental validation in pancreatic cancer cells showed that isorhamnetin exerts antitumor effects, suggesting it may modulate the inflammatory microenvironment connecting CP to PC.

papers.title: Structure based discovery of VMP-7 as a promising GlgE targeting lead against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel drug targets with high specificity and therapeutic potential. Maltosyltransferase (GlgE) is a critical enzyme in the biosynthesis of cytosolic α-glucan, a key component required for maintaining cell wall integrity and intracellular survival of the pathogen. GlgE catalyzes the transfer of maltosyl units from maltose-1-phosphate to elongating α-glucan chains, and its inactivation results in toxic accumulation of metabolic intermediates, ultimately lea
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based drug discovery to identify VMP-7 as a lead compound targeting GlgE, a maltosyltransferase enzyme essential for Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall integrity and survival. GlgE inactivation causes toxic buildup of metabolic intermediates, making it an attractive drug target. VMP-7 shows promise as a starting point for developing new anti-tuberculosis therapeutics.

papers.title: All-atoms MD simulations study of newly designed ciprofloxacin derivatives as potential bacterial DHPS and DNA gyrase inhibitors.
papers.abstract: The widespread use of antibiotics, particularly ciprofloxacin, has accelerated the emergence of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, posing a major public health challenge. Limited investment and declining pharmaceutical interest have slowed the discovery of new antibiotics, contributing to the increasing prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) infections, especially those caused by ESKAPE pathogens. Uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC), a leading cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs), develops multidrug resistance through mechanisms including drug target modification and reduced antibiotic susc
papers.summary: This study uses all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate newly designed ciprofloxacin derivatives as potential inhibitors of bacterial DHPS and DNA gyrase, two key antibiotic targets. The work aims to identify compounds that could overcome multidrug resistance in uropathogenic E. coli by binding these enzymes effectively. It provides computational evidence supporting further experimental testing of these derivatives.

papers.title: Dual targeting of CD244 and CD2 by a viral-immunoevasin-guided engineered CD48-Fc mutant for T- and NK-cell modulation.
papers.abstract: Viruses encode immunoevasins that subvert host co-signaling pathways. CD244:CD48 and CD2:CD58 interactions are critical for NK- and T-cell effector responses. We previously identified a herpesvirus-encoded soluble CD48 homolog that functions as a decoy ligand for CD244 and dampens NK-cell activation. Here, we show that this viral protein, A43, also recognizes CD2, and we used its structural features to engineer human CD48-Fc variants with dual CD244/CD2 specificity. The optimized mutein, C5-Fc, which incorporates twelve A43-guided substitutions predicted by structure-based modeling to enhance
papers.summary: The authors discovered that the herpesvirus immunoevasin A43 binds both CD244 and CD2, and used its structural features to engineer a human CD48-Fc variant (C5-Fc) with dual specificity for these receptors. This engineered mutein can modulate both T- and NK-cell responses, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for immune regulation.

papers.title: Molecular states and interfacial interactions at solid-liquid interfaces: advances and challenges in multimodal characterization.
papers.abstract: Solid-liquid interfaces govern key functions in biosensing, catalysis, energy conversion, drug delivery, and organic electronic devices because molecular adsorption, hydration, charge regulation, and structural reorganization occur within an ultrathin interfacial region. However, these phenomena are intrinsically multiscale and multidimensional, involving strongly coupled variables such as mass, interfacial potential, molecular orientation, viscoelasticity, and local nanoscale heterogeneity. As a result, no single measurement technique can fully describe interfacial states or their dynamics. T
papers.summary: This review discusses how solid-liquid interfaces control processes in biosensing, catalysis, energy conversion, drug delivery, and organic electronics through molecular adsorption, hydration, and charge regulation within an ultrathin region. It argues that because interfacial phenomena are multiscale and multidimensional, no single measurement technique can fully characterize them, and it surveys advances and challenges in multimodal characterization approaches.

papers.title: DDA: a traceable multi-agent framework for automated structure-based drug design.
papers.abstract: Structure-Based Drug Design (SBDD) is a key computational paradigm that uses protein structural information to design and optimize small molecules with desired binding properties. Existing SBDD methods mainly focus on molecular design and often lack the capability to independently conduct downstream evaluation and optimize workflows. Meanwhile, directly applying large language models (LLMs) to molecular design faces challenges such as fragmented execution, limited tool coordination, and insufficient traceability of intermediate decision-making processes. To address these limitations, we propos
papers.summary: The paper introduces DDA, a multi-agent framework that automates structure-based drug design by coordinating specialized agents for molecular generation, evaluation, and optimization. It addresses key limitations of existing methods, such as fragmented execution and poor traceability, by using large language models to manage tool coordination and record intermediate decisions. The framework aims to make automated drug design more transparent and end-to-end.

papers.title: DBP-CanPred: a machine learning model for predicting cancer-causing mutations in DNA-binding proteins.
papers.abstract: The fundamental cellular processes, including transcriptional regulation, chromatin organization, and genome maintenance, are regulated by DNA-binding proteins (DBPs). Mutations in DBPs can alter protein-DNA interactions, leading to tumor development. However, identifying such driver mutations remains a major challenge due to limitations of experimental approaches.
papers.summary: DBP-CanPred is a machine learning model designed to predict cancer-causing mutations specifically in DNA-binding proteins. It addresses the challenge of identifying driver mutations that disrupt protein-DNA interactions, which are difficult to detect experimentally. The tool aims to aid in prioritizing mutations for further study in cancer genomics.

papers.title: Multi-state Structure Prediction of G Protein-Coupled Receptor Proteins via Prompting on AlphaFold.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs), an essential family of transmembrane proteins, widely participate in signal transduction in organisms and have long been recognized as a major class of therapeutic targets. In structure-based drug design, high-resolution structures of GPCRs in both active and inactive states are essential for designing agonists and antagonists, respectively. However, obtaining experimental GPCR structures is costly, while homology modeling and artificial-intelligence-driven approaches including AlphaFold 2 and AlphaFold 3 often show reduced accuracy for active-state conform
papers.summary: This paper presents a method that uses prompt-based adaptation of AlphaFold to predict GPCR structures in multiple functional states, including the active conformations that standard AlphaFold often gets wrong. By improving accuracy for both active and inactive states, the approach aims to better support structure-based design of agonists and antagonists.
